text: GitHub Copilot was first announced on what date?
explanation: It is a code completion assistant for Visual Studio Code, Visual Studio, Neovim, Eclipse and the JetBrains IDEs, built by GitHub with OpenAI. It shipped two years before ChatGPT, which makes it a useful reminder that coding assistants were quietly the first mainstream AI product.

text: Runway AI is a New York company best known for which product category?
explanation: Video, images and other multimedia, through commercial text to video and video generative models. It is one of a cluster of companies, along with Stability AI and Midjourney, that turned generative research into tools filmmakers and designers actually pay for.

text: ElevenLabs, founded in 2022, specialises in which area of AI?
explanation: Speech, and it was founded by Piotr Dąbkowski and Mateusz Staniszewski, who both worked on speech at Google. The company is based in London with offices in New York, Warsaw and San Francisco, which is an unusual arrangement for a company founded by two Polish entrepreneurs and incorporated in the US.

text: Sora, previewed by OpenAI in February 2024, became generally available to which users first?
explanation: Sora generates text to video, and it reached paying ChatGPT subscribers before it reached anyone else. The rollout was staggered by tier and then by region through 2024, which is why a model previewed in February was still gated months later.

text: Google's NotebookLM was renamed in 2025. What is it now called?
explanation: Gemini Notebook, with LM standing for Language Model, and it is a retrieval augmented research and note taking tool. It answers only from documents you give it and cites them, which is the product form that RAG actually looks like when it is aimed at people rather than engineers.

text: What does the LM in the name NotebookLM stand for?
explanation: Language Model, which is the only technical term in the product name. The rest of the name describes what the tool does, which is reading your notes back to you with citations, and the abbreviation is a small joke aimed at people who would recognise it.

text: Which startup launched the screenless AI Pin wearable that flopped in 2024?
explanation: Humane, founded by ex-Apple staffers, shipped the screenless AI Pin in 2024 to dismal reviews over heat, battery and hallucinations. Rabbit is the tempting miss because its R1 flopped the same year, but the pin was Humane's. HP bought most of the company in early 2025 and shut the device down.

text: Which device unveiled at CES in January 2024 promised a large action model that operates apps for you?
explanation: Rabbit unveiled the 199-dollar R1 at CES in January 2024, promising a large action model that clicks through apps for you. The Apple Vision Pro is the tempting miss as the other hyped early-2024 gadget, but the action-model pitch was Rabbit's. Reviewers found a half-baked assistant and called it barely reviewable.

text: Which image service runs through Discord after entering open beta in July 2022?
explanation: Midjourney entered open beta in July 2022 as a bot living entirely inside Discord. Stable Diffusion is the tempting miss because it also arrived that summer, but it runs anywhere while Midjourney stayed Discord-only. Founder David Holz had previously built the Leap Motion controller.

text: Which NotebookLM feature that turns documents into podcast-style chats went viral in September 2024?
explanation: NotebookLM's Audio Overviews, which turn uploaded documents into a two-host podcast chat, went viral in September 2024. Mind Maps is the tempting miss as another NotebookLM view, but the 2024 sensation was audio. Fans shared clips of synthetic hosts bantering over meeting notes and syllabi.

text: Which label had the AI track Heart on My Sleeve pulled from streaming in April 2023?
explanation: The April 2023 track Heart on My Sleeve used AI-cloned vocals of Drake and The Weeknd, and Universal Music Group had it pulled from streaming. Sony Music is the tempting miss as another major label, but UMG acted because both mimicked artists sit on its roster. The anonymous maker ghostwriter still submitted the track for Grammy consideration.

text: How many users did ChatGPT gain in its first two months after launching in November 2022?
explanation: ChatGPT reached about 100 million users within two months of its November 2022 launch, the fastest consumer ramp on record then. Fifty million is the tempting undercount, but outside trackers put the two-month figure at 100 million. UBS analysts called it the fastest-growing consumer app in history.

text: Meta began rolling out a product called Muse to US users on September 8, 2026. What kind of product is it?
options: A personal AI agent you message that works on your apps for you
A multimodal model that generates images and video inside Meta apps
A paid subscription that bundles Meta AI with your Instagram account
A pair of smart glasses with a camera and a built-in voice assistant
answer: A personal AI agent you message that works on your apps for you
explanation: Muse is Meta's personal agent: you tell it what needs doing and it opens a browser, fills in forms, buys things, and comes back to ask before it sends an email or spends money. It runs on Muse Secure VM, a dedicated virtual machine holding both the agent and your data, and you reach it in the Muse app or straight in WhatsApp. The name is deliberately shared with Meta's model line, because Muse runs on Muse Spark, which Meta calls its most capable model to date.

text: Suno launched its v6 music models on September 9, 2026, the first generation it built with music industry partners. Which partners did Suno name?
options: Universal Music Group, Sony Music and Believe
Warner Music Group, BMG and Believe
Warner Music Group, UMG and BMG
answer: Warner Music Group, BMG and Believe
explanation: Suno's own announcement names Warner Music Group, BMG and Believe as the partners v6 was developed with, and says the earlier models would be retired as v6 rolls out. Universal Music Group and Sony are the tempting miss because a player who remembers Suno's copyright fights reaches for the biggest labels rather than the ones that actually signed. The release also came as a set of three models: v6 and v6-wild for paid subscribers, and v6-mini free for everyone.
answerAliases: Warner Music Group, BMG and Believe

text: Manus shipped Manus 2.0 and a separate agent app called Cue on September 28, 2026. In Cue, what does every agent get for itself?
options: A clone of your voice and your writing style
A dedicated GPU and a private server to run on
Its own social media accounts and login details
Its own email, phone number, wallet and computer
answer: Its own email, phone number, wallet and computer
explanation: Cue is a standalone app for personal agents, and Manus gives each one its own email, phone number, wallet and computer so it can message people, pay inside a budget you set, and finish a task on its own machine. A dedicated GPU and a private server is the tempting miss because Manus does sell a Cloud Computer, but that is a separate product you buy for a project. Several agents can also share a group chat and hand work to each other.
answerAliases: its own email, phone number, wallet and computer

text: ByteDance launched Seedance 2.5 on July 31, 2026. Which two of ByteDance's own products did it roll out to on day one?
options: Doubao and Lark, with the API to follow
explanation: Seedance 2.5 went live inside Jimeng AI, ByteDance's video creation app, and Doubao Pro, its paid assistant tier, with API access on BytePlus ModelArk promised for later. CapCut and TikTok are the tempting miss as the two ByteDance apps everyone knows, and Volcengine and ModelArk are the trap because the API only arrived after the consumer launch. The version jump hides the real change: single-pass length doubled from 15 seconds to 30.

text: Black Forest Labs announced FLUX 3 in July 2026, its first model that generates video, and extended the same backbone to predict what a robot should do next. Which carmaker's production network is already testing that action model?
explanation: The action half is called FLUX 3 Action and was built with mimic robotics, whose robots Black Forest Labs says have been tested and deployed at Audi. BFL is the Freiburg startup behind Stable Diffusion and the FLUX image models, and FLUX 3 is the first time it has shipped video at all. Audi's production lab framed the work as solving flexible, soft-body handling that conventionally programmed robot cells cannot handle economically.

source.label: Black Forest Labs on FLUX 3 and mimic robotics

text: Dazzle, the startup founded by Marissa Mayer, launched its first product on September 29, 2026. Unlike most personal assistants, what does Dazzle use to work out who you are?
options: The email and calendar on your work account
The accounts you follow on social media
The voice memos and transcripts on your phone
The photos and screenshots in your camera roll
answer: The photos and screenshots in your camera roll
explanation: Dazzle's launch post is called Pictures, Not Prompts: the camera roll is the context layer, so a photo of a flat tyre becomes a booked repair and a school flyer becomes a calendar entry. Email and calendar is the tempting miss because that is where most personal assistants start, and Mayer's own post argues it skews them toward work. The post opened by noting that around five billion photos would be taken on smartphones that day.

source.label: Dazzle's launch post, Announcing Dazzle: Pictures, Not Prompts

text: Google launched Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS on September 23, 2026, and put each one into a different Google product on day one. The cheaper, high-volume model landed in which product?
explanation: Flash-Lite is the throughput model, built for high-volume dubbing and expressive voice agents at scale, so it is the one Google put into Google Vids, its video creation tool. The creative-direction model, plain Flash, is the one that went into Gemini Notebook instead. Google AI Studio is the tempting miss because it is the other no-code surface, but it is a developer tool: you need an API key to use it.

text: Sonos introduced Sonos 27, the next version of its audio operating system, in September 2026, and previewed its first in-house voice assistant alongside it. What was that in-house assistant built to do?
options: Answer general questions the way Alexa does today
Transcribe and translate speech in real time
Curate music and mood rather than general tasks
Read messages and manage your calendar for you
answer: Curate music and mood rather than general tasks
explanation: Sonos 27voice is deliberately narrow: Sonos describes its own first assistant as built for music and mood curation, not for handling general requests. The general-question distractor is the tempting miss because a speaker that answers questions is what most people picture, and the same release took the opposite route for everything else, adding Sonos 27mcp so an outside assistant such as OpenAI's ChatGPT could drive the system instead. The announcement also folded the Beam Ultra soundbar and Ace Ultra headphones into the portfolio.

text: JetBrains took its AI coding agent Junie out of beta in June 2026. Which protocol did it rebuild the agent's IDE integration on for the general release?
explanation: Junie's general release talks to the IDE over ACP, the same protocol Junie CLI already used, so one agent engine sits behind the AI chat, the Junie tool window and the terminal. Model Context Protocol is the tempting miss because it is the other big agent protocol of 2026, but MCP is about handing a model tools, not plugging an agent into an editor. Language Server Protocol is about completions and navigation.

text: Cursor's Composer 2 and Composer 2.5 coding models were not trained from scratch: Cursor took an open base model from another lab and did its own continued pretraining and reinforcement learning on top. Which lab's open model was that base?
explanation: Both Composer 2 and Composer 2.5 were built on Moonshot AI's open Kimi K2.5 checkpoint, a 1T parameter model that Cursor continued-pretrained on code and then reinforced on long-horizon tasks. The course change came in May 2026, when Cursor said it was training a significantly larger model from scratch with SpaceXAI, using ten times the total compute on Colossus 2. Alibaba and DeepSeek are the tempting misses because both ship strong open coding bases of their own.
